# Core 0.18.0 release preparation

Prepared on 25 October 2026. Scope: Core only.

## Release decision

**The prepared Core product checkpoint passed technical acceptance. Release
after [PR #453](https://github.com/tokentimerch/tokentimer-core/pull/453) is reviewed and merged, and normal CI
passes on the integrated commit.** The PR contains the required native-helper
build correction and workspace-preserving Start over navigation. The evidence
consolidation and TLS-rehearsal follow-up also passed their
recorded checks in [the manifest](evidence/0.18.0/manifest.json). Historical
receipts retain their original tested sources.

## Required fixes

1. **Patched native-helper packaging.** The earlier agent tarball from run
   40142567511 contained Go 1.24.13/1.25.0 executables and failed the configured
   fixed High/Critical gate. Release packaging now pins Go **1.26.10** with
   `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`, verifies the compiler/module/PE and Go architecture/CGO
   settings and hashes of all six actual packed executables, and scans the
   extracted archive. The CMC x509 fallback supported rebuilding; no exploit
   was demonstrated.
2. **Preserve the workspace on Start over.** Preferences reset the selected
   workspace, then navigated to bare `/onboarding`; a fresh browser could
   restore a newer accessible workspace. The fix keeps the exact reset
   workspace in the URL. The same real-page/router/provider regression fails
   against the previous source and passes with the fix; the fixed workspace
   suites passed all 27 cases. All six actual owner-browser journeys passed.
   [Regression proof](https://github.com/tokentimerch/tokentimer-core/blob/85e724eec0b37bc03c22252e7b7bcbef53515281/docs/release/evidence/0.18.0/workspace-reset-regression.json).

## Completed review follow-up

The [CodeQL comment](https://github.com/tokentimerch/tokentimer-core/pull/453#discussion_r4369054039)
was addressed in `927507196afe4b19ec887b30dfd61149dfac9b66`. The loopback
rehearsal now trusts only its locally generated certificate, supplies the
certificate's DNS hostname and enables normal TLS verification. Its exact
fingerprint, HTTP-status and owned-content assertions remain intact.

[Run 40173878344](https://github.com/tokentimerch/tokentimer-core/actions/runs/40173878344)
passed all nine real-TLS/ownership tests on Linux and Windows, including
untrusted-certificate and wrong-hostname rejection before HTTP, plus wrong-pin
and wrong-content rejection. The actual packaged Windows IIS/SAN rehearsal
passed all five checks with verified fixture trust/hostname and complete owned
cleanup. These nine cases were repeated on two platforms; they are not 18
unique features. [CodeQL also passed](https://github.com/tokentimerch/tokentimer-core/actions/runs/40173882807).
The manifest binds the original new receipts, artifact ZIP hashes and exact
source. System trust-store/public-CA and AD CS qualification remain outside
this focused rehearsal. The temporary validation workflow was retired after
success; its executed definition remains in the tested commit.

Normal CI passed 185 frontend files / 2,661 tests, including the new reset
cases; backend coverage passed 2,757 unit and 1,395 integration tests. The
independent Compose integration job also ran its 1,395 cases; overlapping
executions are not summed into unique tests. Server 2025 agent CI passed
1,989 tests with 15 explicit platform/fixture skips recorded in the receipt.
CodeQL passed at the full acceptance checkpoint and the original evidence
commit; the new helper follow-up is tracked separately in the manifest.

The distribution aggregate has seven supporting cohorts: three source agent
modes, three PostgreSQL suites and one Vault adapter. Three operator-package
modes are additional gates. Each lab passed 15 scenarios, yielding 45 source
and 45 package occurrences. The owner journeys prove reset clears completion,
existing verified work does not auto-complete the new session, selection alone
is insufficient, explicit reuse/Continue completes it, reload retains it, and
job/resource/order inventories stay unchanged. Original reports retain their
hash-bound screenshots; the screenshot alone does not establish the sequence.

## Native scope and source accounting

The accepted parallel native cohorts ran on **Windows Server 2022 / en-US /
LocalSystem**: issuance (45), pending/CA (42), templates/uncertain (60),
renewals (24) and recovery (14). Shared scenarios are deduplicated into 169
distinct IDs. The reconciliation preserves their exact original sources,
successful job IDs, ZIP/report/fixture hashes and 13 real-host packaged
operator cases. It carries the release owner's accepted parallel evidence
forward without relabelling the original `native-diagnostic-shard`,
`experimental` and `not-qualified` reports. No stock nine-environment native
collector or broader cross-edition checklist completion is claimed.

Focused later Windows checks ran as administrator on Server 2022/en-US and
remain distinct from that LocalSystem/CA evidence. The original self-signed
IIS fixture receipt excluded trusted-chain validation; the later TLS helper
change does not retroactively alter that receipt. The Linux upgrade rehearsal
does not claim a systemd/Windows installer upgrade, worker maintenance tick
or native CA renewal.

The [source ledger](0.18.0-core-change-ledger.md) preserves the original
82-commit review and nine-commit addendum: **91 commits, 2,049 per-parent file
changes, 1,096 historically touched paths and 1,094 final changed paths**
between v0.17.3 and `fcc681c1` (739 additions, 354 modifications, one removal).
The #420 attribution commit is tree-identical to its parent. Those counts
describe the audited baseline. [Preparation accounting](https://github.com/tokentimerch/tokentimer-core/blob/85e724eec0b37bc03c22252e7b7bcbef53515281/docs/release/evidence/0.18.0/preparation-source-accounting.json)
separately covers the seven preparation commits and 21 paths at `fd441765`;
subsequent evidence consolidation and TLS-helper work have their own diff.

## Cleanup, history and publication

Recorded owned source/package container and network shutdowns succeeded;
named volumes/evidence were retained on disposable hosted runners. Kind was
removed. Upgrade and targeted Windows resources passed their recorded owned
cleanup checks. Earlier failed fixture attempts and the unexplained Vault
startup failure remain in the archive with their original scope and results.

The original four candidate-pinned workflows were retired and normal CI's
main/master trigger restored; their executed definitions remain in history.
Review and merge the PR, run normal CI on the integrated commit, then use a
separately authorized release operation. Fresh publication bytes require
their own observed digests and actual release gates. The previously pushed
beta images predate this preparation. This record creates no release tag,
registry publication or production deployment.
